description: Stacked X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of four as-cast Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr (x = 0, 3, 6, 9) strips. The x-axis is 2θ (degree) running from 30 to 100 with ticks every 10°; the y-axis is Intensity (a.u) with no numerical scale. Four traces are vertically offset for comparison and labelled at the left, bottom to top, 0Cr (black), 3Cr (blue), 6Cr (red) and 9Cr (green). Vertical annotations mark the reflections γ(111), δ(110), γ(200), δ(200), γ(220), δ(211), γ(311) and γ(222). All four patterns show the same set of austenite (γ) and ferrite (δ) reflections: γ(111) near 42–43° is the strongest peak with the δ(110) line immediately to its right (at higher 2θ), γ(200) near 50° is the second strongest, and weaker γ(220), γ(311), γ(222) and δ(200), δ(211) peaks lie between about 65° and 95°. The dominant visual change with Cr content is the relative intensity of δ(110) beside γ(111), which grows from the 0Cr to the 9Cr trace. The figure demonstrates that all strips are two-phase austenite + ferrite with austenite as the major matrix phase, and that Cr addition promotes the ferrite phase.

subfigures.description: XRD pattern of the Cr-free as-cast strip; strongest peak is γ(111) at about 42–43°, with only a weak δ(110) component beside it and a strong γ(200) near 50°; weaker γ(220), γ(311), γ(222) peaks appear at higher 2θ.
XRD pattern of the 3Cr strip, same reflection set as 0Cr, vertically offset; the δ(110) line adjacent to γ(111) is slightly more pronounced than in the 0Cr trace.
XRD pattern of the 6Cr strip; the δ(110) reflection beside γ(111) is clearly separated and relatively stronger than in the 0Cr and 3Cr traces, while γ(200), γ(220), γ(311) and γ(222) remain.

XRD pattern of the 9Cr strip; γ(111) with a distinct δ(110) shoulder/peak to its right is the most prominent feature, and the δ-related reflections are the strongest of the four traces, indicating the largest ferrite contribution.

observations.observation: The figure is a single stacked XRD plot containing four vertically offset traces labelled (bottom to top) 0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr and 9Cr, drawn in black, blue, red and green respectively.
The x-axis is labelled 2θ (degree) and spans 30 to 100 with tick marks at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100; the y-axis is labelled Intensity (a.u) and carries no numerical scale.
Vertical text annotations inside the plot mark the reflections γ(111), δ(110), γ(200), δ(200), γ(220), δ(211), γ(311) and γ(222).

In every trace the γ(111) reflection at about 42–43° (2θ) is the most intense peak and γ(200) at about 50° is the next most intense; the remaining γ(220), γ(311), γ(222) and δ(200), δ(211) peaks are much weaker and lie between roughly 65° and 95° (2θ).
The δ(110) reflection appears immediately to the right (higher 2θ) of γ(111); its relative intensity grows progressively from the 0Cr trace to the 9Cr trace.
The caption states the figure shows X-ray diffraction patterns of as-cast Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr strips.
The citing text states that all Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr strips consist of austenite (γ) and ferrite (δ), with austenite as the major matrix phase.
The citing text states that the δ(110) reflection occurs at 2θ = 44.1° and that its intensity increases with Cr content, meaning Cr addition promotes ferrite formation.
The citing text reports austenite lattice constants of 3.70 Å, 3.56 Å, 3.56 Å and 3.55 Å for the 0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr and 9Cr strips respectively, obtained by JADE analysis of the XRD data.

The citing text reports ferrite fractions of 10.2 vol%, 11.4 vol%, 14.8 vol% and 19.6 vol% for 0Cr, 3Cr, 6Cr and 9Cr, but these values come from the metallographic measurement of Fig. 2 (Gatan Digital Micrograph), not from this XRD figure.

unreadable_items: Y-axis intensity is in arbitrary units with no numerical scale, so absolute or relative peak intensities cannot be quantified from the image
Peak 2θ positions are not printed on the plot apart from the axis ticks; the 44.1° value for δ(110) comes from the citing text, not from the figure
